title: Composing a boolean into an if
idea: Composing functions: a returned True/False can feed an if, or combine with and/or. Compose a decision from smaller checks.

exercises.explanation: is_even(8) returns True, which becomes the if's condition, so it prints even. The returned boolean fed the if.

exercises.prompt: A returned True/False can be used directly as an if's condition.
exercises.explanation: Yes. The if just needs a True/False; a sub-plan that returns one slots right in.
is_even(6) is True and is_positive(6) is True, so True and True is True -> prints both. Two returned booleans composed with and.
is_even(6) is True but is_positive(-6) is False. True and False is False, so it prints not both.
'and' is True only when both sides are True. Composing two returned booleans with and makes a combined rule.

exercises.prompt: REVIEW: why return the booleans instead of printing 'yes'/'no' inside each check?
options: Returned booleans can be combined with and/or and fed to an if
text can be combined with and
exercises.explanation: You can't 'and' two printed words. Returned True/False values combine and drive decisions — that's composable.
is_even(7) is False; not False is True. is_odd reuses is_even and flips it — composition with not.

exercises.prompt: A sub-plan can build a new check by calling another check and flipping it with not.
exercises.explanation: Yes. is_odd = not is_even. Reusing and transforming a returned boolean is composing at the decision level.
is_even(10) is True; not True is False. 10 is not odd, so is_odd(10) is False.

options: Returned booleans compose — feed them to an if, or combine with and/or/not
exercises.explanation: A returned True/False is a value too, so it composes: into an if, with and/or, or flipped with not.
